justification: Standard: this branch includes a real, deliberate production database write (flipping needs_extraction on 54 dcp_chapter_registry rows, explicit user authorization, backed up first) and registers a new live-executable check (DQ-95) that future sessions/CI will run. Not Critical: the write is a status-flag flip, not a content write, and no application code changed -- nothing user-facing is touched. Not Minor: it's a real production write plus a new standing check, not a wording-only change.

pre_impl.existing_data: Reused the exact WHERE clause already used to measure DQ-90 (dcp_chapter_registry, is_active/is_spatial/is_inert/needs_extraction), verified live against production before writing anything -- 54 rows matched, exactly as DQ-90 recorded. No new table, no new column.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: DQ-90 assumed the only blocker was that the extraction pipeline had never been RUN for this council ('the hard part -- getting the documents -- is already done'). Forced this to fail on purpose by actually running the pipeline (--review mode, no writes): the assumption was wrong. The pipeline's own preflight step flagged 52 of 52 processed chapters as SUSPECT (49 preflight_two_column, 3 schema_fail), and manual inspection of one flagged chapter confirmed real, visible text corruption -- not a borderline heuristic false-positive.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The needs_extraction flag flip applies only to Canterbury-Bankstown's 54 already-registered chapters -- no new chapters, no new council, no schema change. DQ-95 is a new row, scoped narrowly to this specific extraction attempt's outcome.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A for the write itself (a status flag, not an external call). The --review run DOES call out to R2 (PDF storage) for each chapter's source PDF -- all 52 downloads succeeded (byte counts logged, ranging 368KB-2.2MB), so this was not an R2/network failure being mistaken for an extraction failure.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: N/A -- nothing was committed to the served regulatory_provisions table. If anything HAD been committed with these SUSPECT flags, a planner using the compliance tool would have been shown corrupted/fabricated-looking rule text (mangled headings, stray page numbers presented as content) as if it were a real DCP clause -- exactly the class of harm this whole session has been about preventing. That is precisely why nothing was committed.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-95 ; python scripts/dq_check.py ; python -m pytest -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-95 fails to connect (exit 2, UNKNOWN) if the database is unreachable -- never reports a false CLEAN. dq_check.py fails if DQ-95's declared status (open) and its live result (nonzero) stop agreeing, or if the ledger and dq_checks.json disagree on which ids exist.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before this branch: DQ-90's own probe (not yet automated, described in prose only) reported 97 chapters with no served content, 54 of them Canterbury-Bankstown, all with needs_extraction=FALSE. After flipping the flag (verified 54/54 matched before the UPDATE, 54/54 rows affected, committed): the same DQ-90-shape query (is_active/NOT is_spatial/NOT is_inert/NOT needs_extraction/no served provision) now reads 43 live-verified -- down from 97, with a live per-council breakdown matching DQ-90's own named 20-council list exactly (northern_beaches 3, fairfield 3, liverpool 3, ... cumberland 1). This proves the flag flip touched exactly the intended 54 rows and nothing else. dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-95 reads count=54 (all still stuck, none successfully extracted) -- correctly RED, matching the real, observed pipeline failure this session found by actually running the extraction (not assumed from the flag state alone). python scripts/dq_check.py: PASSED, 99 rows (98 + this session's DQ-95), 0 red, coverage intact. Full pytest suite: 4967 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed -- unchanged, since no application code was touched.

functions.name: PROBES["DQ-95"]
functions.input: none beyond the standing --id DQ-95 CLI arg
functions.output: count of canterbury_bankstown chapters with needs_extraction=TRUE AND last_extracted_at IS NULL -- 0 would mean every queued chapter was eventually extracted successfully; currently 54 (all of them, since none has been committed)
functions.if_none: N/A -- exits 2/UNKNOWN via the shared run() harness if the database is unreachable, same as every other probe in this file, never a false CLEAN

break_it.scenario: The needs_extraction=TRUE flag flip on 54 rows could accidentally cause the pipeline's SCHEDULED, automated sweep (the --all mode used for the 'quarterly re-extract-all detector cadence') to pick these 54 chapters up on its next scheduled run and commit the known-SUSPECT extraction output to production, since nothing about the flag itself prevents that -- only running with --review manually does.
break_it.what_happens: If a scheduled --all run (without --review) fires before someone builds a real two-column fix, the exact garbled content this session deliberately kept out of production would get committed automatically, and DQ-90/DQ-95's own prose would be the only warning anyone had.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated at the mechanism level -- there is no code-level guard preventing a scheduled --all run from committing SUSPECT output; the pipeline's own design is 'commit unless a human intervenes', which is exactly what DQ-92 already documented as a standing risk for this repo's review-queue model generally. Named here explicitly rather than assumed safe: whoever picks up the two-column fix (or decides to skip Canterbury-Bankstown) should check whether any scheduled extraction job runs --all without --review before that decision is made, since this branch's flag flip is what makes these 54 chapters newly eligible for a future --all sweep to reach.
break_it.repro: grep for how --all is invoked in any cron/scheduled config (not done in this session -- named as the open question, not investigated).

break_it.scenario: This branch was originally started as uncommitted changes on fix/fabricated-compliance-fallback (an unrelated, already-CI-passed branch) before being noticed and moved.
break_it.what_happens: Committing DQ-90/DQ-95 work onto that branch would have silently bundled two unrelated changes into one PR, and re-triggered CI on a PR that had already passed review for a narrower, already-understood scope.
break_it.how: Caught before committing: `git status --short` on that branch showed the 3 unrelated files staged. Moved via `git stash push -u` with a unique, descriptive tag (not a bare stash, per this repo's shared-stash-stack convention), a fresh worktree/branch cut from updated origin/main, and `git stash apply` (not pop) by exact SHA. The apply produced real merge conflicts in 2 of 3 files (this branch's origin/main snapshot predates a second, still-unmerged PR's DQ-91/DQ-94 changes) -- resolved by keeping this branch's own DQ-90/DQ-95 content and the ORIGINAL upstream DQ-91 text, deliberately NOT importing the other PR's DQ-94 addition here (it will arrive naturally when that PR merges). Verified post-resolution: 0 leftover conflict markers in any of the 3 files, valid JSON, dq_check.py PASSED, full pytest suite unchanged.
break_it.repro: grep -c "^<<<<<<<\|^=======\|^>>>>>>>" on all 3 touched files -- 0 in each, confirmed after resolution.

break_it.scenario: The pre-write backup of the 54 dcp_chapter_registry rows was initially written only to a session-specific scratchpad temp directory, not committed to the repository -- if that temp directory were cleaned up before anyone needed to restore the pre-flip state, the backup would be gone.
break_it.what_happens: The CLAUDE.md rule 'create backup before ANY database operation' would have been satisfied only in the narrow, in-session sense, not durably.
break_it.how: Copied into data/db_rollback_backups/ (this repo's existing, tracked convention for exactly this purpose -- confirmed via `git check-ignore`, unlike the separate gitignored `backups/` directory) as dcp_chapter_registry_canterbury_bankstown_pre_flag_flip_2026-09-05.json (35KB, well under the ~600KB norm for that directory). Committed with this branch.
